question.text: Which section of the Income Tax Act provides relief to a taxpayer where India does NOT have a Double Tax Avoidance Agreement with the foreign country?

explanation.text: The Logic: Section 91 of the Income Tax Act provides unilateral relief from double taxation. It applies where India does not have a Double Tax Avoidance Agreement with the foreign country in which the income was earned. The provision allows a resident Indian to claim a deduction from Indian tax equal to the lower of (a) the foreign tax actually paid or (b) the Indian tax payable on the doubly taxed income, so the same income is not taxed twice purely because no treaty exists. The Trap: Section 90 provides DTAA relief where India does have a treaty with the other country — the opposite scenario. Section 90A deals with agreements between specified associations, not government-to-government DTAAs. Section 92 covers transfer pricing for related-party cross-border transactions, not double-taxation relief. Note: The cited NISM Series X-B Investment Adviser Level 2 workbook pages reviewed in the audit explain that DTAAs avoid double taxation by allocating taxing rights or allowing residence-state credit for source-state taxes, but they do not mention Section 91 or unilateral relief where India lacks a DTAA on the pages checked. The framing above reflects general Indian Income Tax Act knowledge.
